Sol / xhigh · Four task conditions · 15 September 2026

Tissue under
the wrong label

Sol missed 21 mL of pancreatic tissue assigned to the duodenum while checking every organ. A fresh attempt found it when asked to inspect just those two organs, using the same scans and labels.

Organ masks mark which tissue belongs to each organ. This experiment changes the labels while keeping the CT scan unchanged.

21.04 mLtissue reassigned in the partial case

Same CTall source image samples retained
01 / The task

Find the tissue
under the wrong name.

Give the agent existing organ masks, their proposed names, full CT and tools to render views. Ask which masks contain at least 5 mL of another organ.

Here, part of the source pancreas is transferred into its neighbor’s label. The remaining pancreas and the enlarged duodenum both retain plausible overall shapes. The transfer spans 45 × 37.5 × 67.5 mm.

A small, exact deliverable

Report the host mask, the included organ, and one point inside the wrongly assigned tissue. The point tolerance is 3 mm. No contour reconstruction is required.

The error is synthetic and its identity comes from the source mask. The CT and total labeled tissue are unchanged; the other 11 organ masks are unchanged.

Image counts are returned returned images, not tiles within a sheet. Command counts include recovered failed commands.

Every run used gpt-5.6-sol / xhigh, Codex 0.154.0, a fresh session, zero retries, and allowances of 1,800 seconds, four CPUs and 4 GiB RAM. Peak CPU/RAM use was not measured. All eight oracle/no-op controls behaved as expected. Independent source-grid checks and scoring replay agree with the outcomes.

03 / The agent at work

Measure. Look. Reconsider.

A reconstruction from public progress messages, executed commands, returned images and final answers. Interpretations are marked separately.

1. Read the scene

Existing masks, proposed names, coordinates and CT.

2. Measure and render

Python geometry and intensity checks; targeted image sheets.

3. Assess anatomy

Compare shape, continuity and neighbors; request further views.

4. Return a finding

Host, included organ and interior point—or an empty list.

The model acts as a controller of this tool loop. No specialist medical inference model or new training was invoked in these traces. Existing segmentations were supplied; Sol’s task was to audit their ownership.

M02 / All 13 labels present · audit every mask

A full inspection still misses the transferred tissue

Miss

21.04 mL of source pancreas is reassigned to the duodenum mask. A 38.38 mL pancreatic remnant remains separately labeled. The CT is unchanged.

404 s · 27 images · 10,593 output tokens

  1. Establish plausibility

    Read the proposed labels and view the whole scene, then all 13 dedicated CT previews. The first public assessment is that the gross anatomy looks plausible.

    Trace steps 7, 9, 10, 15, 16, 17

  2. Measure and inspect the relevant pair

    Map cropped masks into CT coordinates; compute intensity distributions, volume, six-neighbor connected components and pairwise overlap. Request additional axial, coronal and sagittal sheets containing pancreas, duodenum and stomach. The enlarged duodenum remains one connected component.

    Trace steps 18, 19, 20, 21, 23

  3. Accept the local appearance, expand the sweep

    The public assessment accepts the pancreatic head-to-tail course as consistent with its label. Inspection then moves through liver, vessels, stomach, kidneys, spleen and adrenals. No included pancreatic region is reported.

    Trace steps 24, 25, 26, 27, 28

  4. Write an empty answer

    Explicitly conclude that no inclusion meets the 5 mL threshold, write an empty findings list and validate its format. The grader fails detection; point localization is never reached.

    Trace steps 30, 31, 32, 33
So far, the gallbladder’s low attenuation and the pancreas’ head-to-tail course are consistent with their labels; neither is an obvious mixed-organ error.Public assessment before the remaining-organ sweep · step 24

Recovered from missing SciPy and an attempt to index full CT with a cropped mask. Subsequent calculations used NumPy/Python and coordinate transforms.

Interpretation

The trace is consistent with accepting plausible labels without resolving the ownership error at their interface. It does not support an explanation based on never viewing the affected organs: all three CT planes were inspected. A single run cannot identify the internal cause of the miss.

M01 / 12 labels present · audit every mask

A missing label prompts an anatomical search

Pass

The separate pancreas mask is removed and its tissue is incorporated into duodenum: 59.35 mL newly added. Both the missing-class clue and the larger abnormal extent differ from M02.

349 s · 26 images · 15,102 output tokens

  1. Generate leads

    Notice the absent pancreas label and an unusual upper aortic loop. Explicitly treat absence as a reason to search neighboring masks, rather than a finding by itself. Review every target preview and screen geometry and CT intensity.

    Trace steps 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17

  2. Identify two anatomies in one mask

    Targeted CT sheets show an upper part of o327 following the pancreatic gland while the lower duodenal C-loop remains. The public report identifies this as the inclusion. Later views compare the suspect tissue with stomach and splenic-vein context.

    Trace steps 20, 21, 24, 26, 27, 30

  3. Quantify a substantial region

    Count mask voxels in selected physical-coordinate regions. For example, the subset at z ≥ 357 mm and x ≥ 5 mm contains 13.932 mL. This measures the selected mask region; interpreting it as pancreas still depends on the anatomical review.

    Trace steps 25, 28, 29, 30

  4. Choose and validate a witness

    Use erosion and local CT statistics to select a point inside the suspected gland. Check mask membership, CT coordinates and JSON format. Return one pancreas-in-duodenum finding, with no extras; the reference accepts the point.

    Trace steps 28, 31, 32, 33, 34
The duodenum host is a confirmed concern: its superior component follows the solid pancreatic gland across several slices, while its inferior C-shaped bowel remains present.Public finding after the targeted gastrointestinal sheets · step 21

Interpretation

This pass combines a useful search cue, relative anatomical position and continuity across slices, followed by numerical localization. It is not a label-count-only solution. The comparison cannot separate the effect of an absent class from the effect of a larger, more recognizable inclusion.

N01 / Original 13 masks · audit every mask

Two asserted errors are withdrawn after further checks

Pass

Original source masks are retained. The correct output is an explicit empty findings list. This tests false alarms under the same broad audit instructions.

453 s · 31 images · 11,864 output tokens

  1. Investigate unusual appearances

    Review all target previews, then additional pancreas, gallbladder, stomach and liver sheets. Compute connected components and spatial summaries. The pancreas/duodenum pair and large vessels initially attract attention.

    Trace steps 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 20, 22, 24

  2. Assert two provisional errors

    A public progress message states that the pancreas includes duodenum and the gallbladder follows liver tissue. These claims would be false positives against this unchanged-source key. They are not the final answer.

    Trace steps 25

  3. Gather counterevidence

    Measure CT intensity in correctly registered masks and along their slice-wise course; view pancreas and duodenum together in all three planes; compute cross-mask face adjacency. Gallbladder mean intensity is 9.9 HU versus liver 56.9 HU. These are supporting measurements, not an anatomical classifier by themselves.

    Trace steps 26, 27, 28, 29, 30

  4. Revise and clear the case

    Finish the vessel and solid-organ sweep. The final public assessment says the suspicious gastrointestinal shapes resolve as normal adjacent structures. Write and validate an empty findings list. Both earlier claims are absent from the final answer.

    Trace steps 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 37, 38, 39

Interpretation

The successful negative result came after a visible revision, not uniform confidence throughout. Additional checks preceded that revision, but the public record does not specify which single observation caused it. This was the longest run and returned the most images; more work did not mean a harder positive case.

F01 / M02 data unchanged · audit two masks

A closer look finds the tissue between the organs

Pass

Every M02 image, mask, CT sample, helper and reference-key byte is retained. The prompt narrows the audit to o327 (duodenum) and o589 (pancreas); other anatomy remains context. This follow-up was declared after the initial positive-case results.

351 s · 17 images · 12,009 output tokens

  1. Examine the two targets together

    Read the metadata and four ready previews. Compute target components and overlaps, then request three-plane CT sheets and four rotated 3-D views. The early public assessment still calls the large-scale shapes coherent.

    Trace steps 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19

  2. Continue past global plausibility

    Explicitly inspect the shared interface at finer spacing. Render each mask separately at 4.5 mm axial steps, inspect all-mask context, tabulate 2-D components slice by slice, and request tighter three-plane interface views.

    Trace steps 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25

  3. Localize the wrongly assigned gland

    The final public finding identifies pancreatic head/uncinate tissue inside o327 while accepting the remaining o589 tissue as pancreas. Count selected suspect regions, including a central upper subset of 9.993 mL; use erosion depth to choose an interior voxel.

    Trace steps 26, 27, 28

  4. Verify the point and return one finding

    Check that the selected point lies inside o327 and outside o589, and map it to a CT voxel. Return [-22.9, -199.9, 324.7] LPS mm. Independent scoring places it 0.016 mm from an included source voxel centre.

    Trace steps 29, 30, 31, 32

Recovered from missing SciPy by implementing connected-component and erosion operations with NumPy/Python.

Interpretation

The observable distinction is continued inspection of tissue ownership after the overall shapes looked plausible. This weakens a claim of general inability to recognize the anatomy. Scope provides a localization hint, and fresh-run variation remains possible; the contrast does not prove an attention mechanism.

04 / Takeaways

Check which organ the tissue belongs to.

Where the agent looks matters.

M02 saw the relevant pair and accepted its appearance. F01 called the global shapes coherent too, then continued into finer interface checks and found the inclusion. Narrower scope supplies an attention cue.

The clean case shows a useful change of mind.

N01 publicly asserted two errors before later clearing the case correctly. That makes the additional checks and willingness to revise as interesting as the final score.

More images did not guarantee a better answer.

The focused pass received 17 images versus 27 in the broad miss. It took 13% less agent time and 17% fewer input tokens, but produced 13% more output. Efficiency remains an experiment to test.

These selected, single-run contrasts do not establish a failure rate or isolate a causal mechanism. F01 was a declared post-result follow-up that explicitly narrowed the audit to the affected pair. No additional trials were run for this presentation.
